title: Ines and the Letter
premise: Felix Lockridge, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has kept them professionally invisible, receives two letters mailed the same day from the same dying woman: one confessing to a thirty-year-old arson that killed her business partner, the other promising Felix a fortune if they can prove she didn't do it. Following the paper trail to the decaying seaside town of Marrow Bay, Felix discovers their own name woven into the old alibis—a relative they never knew they had. As the town's loyalists close ranks and the last witness begins forgetting everything, Felix must choose between protecting a found family's comfortable lie and exposing the truth. In the end, Felix closes the case by proving both letters true: the confession was written to shield a daughter, and the promise was written to free her—resolving it with an inheritance of memory rather than money.
about_author: Zephyrine Almeida is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved claims in coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people whose careful lives are undone by paper.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Felix Lockridge's POV. A meticulous investigator receives twin letters from a stranger named Vera Quill—one confessing to murder, one offering payment for innocence—written in identical handwriting. The emotional beat is unease: for the first time, Felix's perfect memory registers something it cannot file away.

chapters.title: The Case That Closed Itself
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Flashback establishes Felix's reputation and self-imposed invisibility, including the rule never to investigate anything connected to their own past. The letters violate that rule because the return address is Marrow Bay—the town on Felix's only unexplained childhood document. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Arrival at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix arrives in Marrow Bay posing as a claims auditor and finds a town preserved like evidence: same faces, same silences. Vera Quill is alive but fading in a care home, refusing visitors. Beat: the uncanny feeling of walking through a memory that isn't yours.

chapters.title: The Cannery Fire, 1994
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, interleaved with archival records. Felix reconstructs the fire that killed partner Edmund Hale and closed the Quill-Hale cannery; the official verdict was accidental, Vera's letter says otherwise. Beat: the thrill of a puzzle with a wrong-shaped piece.

chapters.title: A Daughter Who Answers Doors
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix meets Ruth Quill, Vera's protective daughter, who runs the rebuilt cannery and mistakes Felix for an insurance vulture. Their sparring reveals Ruth knows more about the letters than she admits. Beat: attraction sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: Alibi Number One
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The first alibi—three townspeople swearing Vera was at a church supper—checks out perfectly, too perfectly, each account matching word for word. Felix recognizes coached testimony. Beat: the investigator's cold delight curdling into anger.

chapters.title: What the Photograph Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using photographic recall on a 1994 newspaper photo, Felix spots a child in the background wearing a locket identical to their own inherited one. The chapter ends with Felix admitting aloud, alone, that Marrow Bay may be theirs. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Ruth's Version
chapters.summary: Ruth Quill's POV. Ruth explains why the town lies: Vera confessed privately years ago to protect someone, and the community agreed to bury it. She warns Felix off, but slips them Vera's old ledger. Beat: loyalty presented as love, and as a cage.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The ledger's final pages are razored out, but pressure indentations survive. Felix reconstructs entries suggesting payments made after the fire—to someone still alive. Beat: the hunter realizing the trail leads forward, not back.

chapters.title: Alibi Number Two
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A second alibi surfaces, this one placing Edmund Hale alive an hour after the fire's official start time. If true, the death certificate is false—and so is half the case. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by the sense of being managed.

chapters.title: The Man Who Keeps the Clocks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix tracks down Silas Marsh, the retired harbormaster who repaired every clock in town, including the cannery's stopped one frozen at the fire's start. Silas recognizes Felix's surname and goes pale. Beat: the past reaching out and touching the present.

chapters.title: Silas Talks Around the Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Silas then Felix. Silas reveals he reset the cannery clock after the fire on Vera's instruction, buying someone an alibi—but refuses to say who, invoking a debt owed to Felix's mother. Beat: revelation withheld, connection confirmed.

chapters.title: My Mother's Town
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts their own sealed adoption records and realizes their mother grew up in Marrow Bay, entangled with the Quills and Hales. The investigation becomes personal inheritance. Beat: grief for a history that was hidden to protect them.

chapters.title: Vera, Awake for Ten Minutes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix finally reaches Vera during a lucid interval. She gives him a riddle—'the confession is the lie, the promise is the truth, and both were for you'—before slipping away again. Beat: tenderness and frustration in equal measure.

chapters.title: Someone Burns the Archive
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The county records room holding the original fire files goes up in flames hours after Felix requests them. Arson again—someone is repeating history to stop Felix. Beat: fear, and the realization Felix is now inside the story.

chapters.title: Ruth Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Torn between the town's pact and her mother's obvious wish, Ruth gives Felix the torn ledger pages she's kept hidden since Vera's first diagnosis. They name a beneficiary: F. Lockridge. Beat: betrayal transformed into trust.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Date
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Forensic detail: the 'promise' letter was written decades ago and held by a lawyer, released upon Vera's terminal diagnosis—meaning Vera planned this handoff for years, choosing Felix specifically. Beat: awe at being seen by a stranger who knew them completely.

chapters.title: Alibi Number Three
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The final alibi collapses: the church supper log shows Vera left early, and the person she covered for was Edmund Hale himself—he wasn't murdered; he staged his death and fled, and Vera's 'confession' was blackmail insurance against his return. Beat: the whole board flipping at once.

chapters.title: Edmund Comes Home
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The ledger payments traced, Felix finds Edmund Hale living under a new name two towns over, drawn back by news of Vera's decline. Confrontation: he offers Felix hush money and a family explanation. Beat: temptation offered by the person least entitled to give it.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Loaded Word
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth learns her father is alive and that her mother spent thirty years paying for his freedom while the town lied to protect Ruth's inheritance and name. She must decide what loyalty owes the dead versus the living. Beat: heartbreak becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Reading of Both Letters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At Vera's bedside, with Ruth and the town's elders present, Felix reads both letters aloud and lays out the truth: no murder, one cowardice, one long sacrifice. Vera dies peacefully within the hour, having heard herself absolved accurately. Beat: catharsis; truth delivered as mercy.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Memory
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, coda. Felix declines the money, keeps the letters, and files a report closing the 1994 claim as 'resolved—no crime.' Staying in Marrow Bay a while longer, Felix accepts belonging instead of invisibility. Final beat: the investigator who remembers everything finally chooses what's worth keeping.
